findings.summary: supersededByNewerRun compares `o.workflowName === c.workflowName`, so two rows that both lack a workflowName count as the same workflow. It also takes `runId` from `detailsUrl`, and any GitHub App installed on the repo can set that URL. A check-run could therefore claim an Actions run id and suppress a red row in reconciler routing. Impact is low: this only affects routing, and the merge gate (merge-if-eligible) matches on app id, workflow_id and check_suite_id from the REST API. To harden it, require `c.workflowName !== undefined` before dropping a row.
